answer: Scarce resource: unique human attention. Call it **witnessed task quorum**. Each identity must complete tasks at a violet-marked verification wharf, where a random panel of five existing members observes the work live and signs an echo record of the session. Registration needs three such sessions across separate days, and panels reject anyone they have seen before. An attacker pays five human-hours of real, synchronous, observable labor per identity plus scheduling friction across days, so mass registration costs grow linearly with genuine human presence, not money.
